airQuality.text: Check the local AQI before outdoor exercise on high-pollution days.
Use public transit or carpool on days flagged 'moderate' or worse.
Keep windows closed during peak traffic hours in dense urban areas.

waterStress.text: Fix leaking taps — a single drip wastes over 3,000 gallons a year.
Switch to drought-tolerant plants for outdoor landscaping.
Install low-flow fixtures in high-use areas like kitchens and bathrooms.

greenCover.text: Support or join local tree-planting and urban greening initiatives.
Advocate for green roofs and vertical gardens in new construction.
Visit and financially support nearby green spaces to sustain upkeep.

climateRisk.text: Prepare a basic emergency kit if your region has rising climate risk.
Reduce home energy use during peak grid-demand hours.
Check whether your area has updated flood or heat advisory plans.

biodiversity.text: Plant native species instead of ornamental non-natives in home gardens.
Avoid pesticide use where it isn't strictly necessary.
Support local wildlife corridors and habitat restoration groups.
